text_en: South Korea's September exports extended strong growth, with global AI demand continuing to drive semiconductor exports, leading the market to expect that this heavily trade-dependent economy will remain resilient despite rising interest rates. Data released by Korea Customs on Thursday showed that, adjusted for working days, South Korea's September exports rose 104.9% year-on-year. Korea Customs said that in the first nine months of 2026, South Korea's exports reached 814.5 billion US dollars, surpassing the 800 billion US dollar mark for the first time and hitting a record high. The chip boom is also changing the South Korean government's fiscal position. South Korea expects national tax revenue to reach a record 478.6 trillion won (about 353 billion US dollars) this year, up 28% from 2025, mainly driven by semiconductor company profits, special dividends from chip companies, active stock markets and a consumption recovery.
